targets.title: Reading literary fiction improves theory of mind.
targets.evidence_quote:
In the present article, we report the findings of four replications of Kidd and Castano (
Citation
2013).
targets.outcome_quote: In each of these four experiments, we found no significant effects of reading literary fiction on mentalising performance. Moreover, analysing the combined data of four experiments with a total of N 1,017 participants yielded no significant effects of reading literary fiction. The present results thus fail to confirm the notion that a single session of reading literary fiction can prime enhanced mentalising performance.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall conclusion rejects the central priming effect named in the title across all four experiments. The replicated familiarity correlation is discussed as a check on procedural validity, rather than changing the verdict on the priming replication.

reasoning: Four new-sample experiments explicitly re-test Kidd and Castano. Original Experiment 1 and Experiment 3 are explicitly mapped to replication Experiments 1 and 4. Panero is a parallel prior replication, not a target. Prior correlational literature motivates the familiarity measure; the stated replication aim targets the causal priming finding.
